summary.short: Proposed EU regulation to expand cloud and AI capacity: Leadership Initiatives, national strategies, data centre acceleration zones with faster permits, four Union assurance levels for cloud services sold to public bodies, public-order procurement rules, a public-sector cloud federation and Commission joint procurement. Applies one year after entry into force.
summary.long: The proposal sets up Cloud and AI Leadership Initiatives with eight operational objectives implemented through grand challenges in Annex I, requires each Member State to establish Centres for AI and a national cloud and AI strategy within a year, and lets the Commission recognise frontier AI priority projects involving at least three Member States, to which the Union and Member States allocate computing resources. Member States deploying data centre capacity must designate acceleration zones within six months, issue an aggregated baseline permit per zone, designate single information points and decide permits within 12 months; the Commission may designate data centre strategic projects meeting two of five criteria. A cloud sovereignty framework defines four Union assurance levels (Annex II): level 1 by self-assessment, levels 2-4 by annual independent audit, recognised by national competent authorities with Union-wide peer review and a public repository. Criteria escalate from Union establishment and data location to Union-citizen personnel, cybersecurity certification and absence of third-country control. Public bodies must buy level 1 services, or levels 2-4 for public-order activities identified in risk assessments, with derogations. Member States set penalties; authorities may order cessation and impose fines; recipients may claim compensation.

territorial_scope.description: European Union; directly applicable in all Member States. Cloud assurance criteria require Union establishment, with level 3 open to providers controlled from associated third countries named by implementing act.

evidence.quote: This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.

obligations.summary: Each Member State must establish Experience and Acceleration Centres for AI, building on European digital innovation hubs, to support AI adoption, upskilling and scale-ups.
obligations.applies_from: date of application (entry into force + 1 year)

evidence.quote: Each Member State shall establish Experience and Acceleration Centres for AI (‘Centres for AI’).

obligations.summary: Member States must establish national cloud and AI strategies with at least the contents in Art. 7(2) (adoption, data centre capacity, AI factories, procurement, open stacks, data access).

evidence.quote: The national strategies shall include at least the following:

obligations.summary: Member States must notify their strategies to the Commission within three months of adoption and reassess them at least every three years against KPIs.

evidence.quote: The Member States shall notify the Commission of their national strategies within three months of their adoption.

obligations.summary: The Union and Member States must allocate sufficient AI computing resources to frontier AI priority projects within available capacity; the Union must at least match Member State contributions within its EuroHPC access-time share.
obligations.conditional_on: Project recognised as frontier AI priority project under Art. 8

evidence.quote: T he Union shall at least match the AI computing resources contributed by Member States to frontier AI priority projects

obligations.summary: Member States where data centre capacity is being deployed must designate at least one data centre acceleration zone, considering site size, grid and network capacity, waste-heat reuse, permitting, brownfield preference and sustainability.
obligations.conditional_on: Data centre capacity is being deployed within the Member State's territory

evidence.quote: Where data centre capacity is being deployed with in the territory of a Member State, that Member State shall designate at least one data centre acceleration zone

obligations.summary: Where appropriate, Member States must analyse energy needs and GHG impacts of acceleration zones (reviewed every three years) and ensure TSO and DSO network development plans take that analysis into account.
obligations.conditional_on: Where appropriate to facilitate the development of acceleration zones

evidence.quote: ensure that the network development plans prepared by transmission system operators pursuant to Article 51 of Directive (EU) 2019/944

obligations.summary: Member States must make spatial planning data available to data centre operators, combine SEA and habitats assessments of plans, and involve all relevant authorities, electronic communications operators, TSOs and DSOs when designating zones.

evidence.quote: Member States shall ensure that all relevant spatial planning data are available to data centre operators .

obligations.summary: When setting sustainability requirements for data centres in acceleration zones, Member States must use the KPIs of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364, and must allocate zone resources on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms without speculative reservation or foreclosure.

evidence.quote: Member States shall ensure that the allocation and use of resources within acceleration zones takes place on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms

obligations.summary: Member States must designate single information points that assist data centre operators in acceleration zones, on request, with all authorisations over the project lifecycle (operators have a right to this assistance).

evidence.quote: For that purpose, Member States shall designate one or more single information points for data centre operators of data centre projects in acceleration zones .

obligations.summary: For each acceleration zone, Member States must carry out zone-level assessments and issue an aggregated baseline permit covering the permits needed by data centre projects there, excluding installation-specific permits.

evidence.quote: For each designated acceleration zone, Member States shall prepare and issue an aggregated baseline permit authorising the deployment of data centres in that acceleration zone .

obligations.summary: Member States must process applications efficiently and decide permits for data centre projects in acceleration zones within 12 months of a comprehensive application, and give them the highest national significance status where national law has one.

evidence.quote: Member States shall ensure that administrative applications related to the planning, construction and the operation of data centre deployed in acceleration zones are processed in an efficient, transparent and timely manner.

obligations.summary: Data centres in acceleration zones need additional permits only for activities outside the zone's aggregated baseline permit; their projects count as strategic projects under the pending environmental-assessment regulation.
obligations.conditional_on: Data centre deployed in a designated acceleration zone

evidence.quote: Data centres deployed in acceleration zones shall be required to obtain additional permits only for activities falling outside the aggregated baseline permit referred to in paragraph 2.

obligations.summary: Applicants for data centre strategic project designation must supply information showing the criteria are met and substantiating the project's predicted lifetime, which sets the designation's duration.
obligations.conditional_on: Applying in a Commission open call for strategic projects

evidence.quote: In its proposal, the applicant shall provide all the necessary and relevant information to demonstrate that the project fulfils the relevant criteria.

obligations.summary: The Commission must identify and monitor Union compute capacity, demand for data centre capacity and the capacity gap and underserved areas.

evidence.quote: t he Commission shall identify and monitor:

obligations.summary: The Commission must review Annexes II (assurance criteria) and III (audit evidence) at least every 18 months.

evidence.quote: T o ensure Annex II and Annex III rem ain up to date with new legal or technical developments , the Commission shall review them at least every 18 months .

obligations.summary: A cloud computing service provider seeking recognition at a Union assurance level must apply to the competent authority of establishment with the required evidence (statement of conformity for level 1; audit report, positive opinion and audit evidence for levels 2-4).
obligations.applies_from: date of application (entry into force + 1 year)
obligations.conditional_on: Provider aims to be recognised as offering a Union assurance level (required to supply Union entities and public sector bodies, Arts 16(1), 30)

evidence.quote: A c loud computing service provider that aims to be recognised as offering a Union assurance level , shall submit a n application for recognition to the national competent authority of establishment .

obligations.summary: The evaluating national competent authority must assess applications within 60 days and either notify a draft recognition decision for a 60-day Union review, request more information, or reject after hearing the provider; it must consider objections from other authorities.

evidence.quote: t he evaluating national competent authority shall assess the evidence submitted pursuant to paragraphs 3 or 4 and shall either :

obligations.summary: On referral of a disputed draft recognition, the Commission must assess it and adopt a binding decision on whether the recognition may be adopted.
obligations.conditional_on: A national competent authority refers a maintained draft decision under Art. 17(10)

evidence.quote: T he Commission shall adopt a binding decision determining whether the evaluati ng national competent authority may adopt the recognition decision .

obligations.summary: Providers seeking level 1 recognition must self-assess against the level 1 criteria and issue an EU statement of conformity, assuming responsibility for compliance.
obligations.conditional_on: Seeking Union assurance level 1

evidence.quote: shall carry out a c onformity self-assessment of compliance with the criteria for Union assurance level 1 set out in Annex II .

obligations.summary: Providers must make their EU statement of conformity publicly available.
obligations.conditional_on: Provider has issued an EU statement of conformity (level 1)

evidence.quote: The cloud computing service provider shall make the EU statement of conformity publicly available.

obligations.summary: Providers seeking levels 2, 3 or 4 must undergo, at their own expense, independent third-party audits by auditing organisations meeting the independence, expertise and ethics conditions of Art. 20(4), meeting all lower-level criteria too.
obligations.conditional_on: Seeking Union assurance level 2, 3 or 4

evidence.quote: shall undergo at their own expense, independent third-party au dit s to obtain an audit report and an audit opinion from an auditing organisation .

obligations.summary: Audited providers must cooperate with auditors, give access to data and premises, answer questions, and not hamper or unduly influence the audit.
obligations.conditional_on: Undergoing a level 2-4 audit

evidence.quote: Audited providers shall refrain from hampering, unduly influencing or undermining the performance of the audit.

obligations.summary: Recognised level 2-4 providers must submit the audit report and positive opinion annually for review of continued compliance; the auditor may confirm, update or revoke them.
obligations.conditional_on: Holding a positive audit opinion for level 2, 3 or 4

evidence.quote: which shall assess the continued compliance of the audited service with the applicable criteria set out in Annex II.

obligations.summary: Recognised providers must notify the auditing organisation and the competent authority as soon as possible of any information or material change that may affect the audit opinion or recognition.
obligations.conditional_on: Provider's service is recognised under Art. 17

evidence.quote: the recognised cloud computing service provider shall , as soon as possible , notify the auditing organisation and the national competent authority of establishment.

obligations.summary: Level 1: provider established in the Union; infrastructure and assets (incl. subcontractors') located in the Union and customer data, metadata and telemetry kept exclusively in the Union, unless the public sector body explicitly requires otherwise; traceable out-of-Union support.
obligations.conditional_on: Recognition at Union assurance level 1

evidence.quote: the cloud computing service provider is established in the Union;

obligations.summary: Level 1: state-of-the-art cybersecurity, full transparency and due diligence on subcontractors, and (if third-country controlled) a guarantee that no third-country law requires reporting unexploited vulnerabilities to its authorities.
obligations.conditional_on: Recognition at Union assurance level 1

evidence.quote: the cloud computing service provider demonstrates that the service complies with the state-of-the-art cybersecurity standards;

obligations.summary: Levels 2-4: provider and involved subcontractors established in the Union; infrastructure, assets and personnel located in the Union; customer data exclusively in the Union (for level 4, data identified as sensitive, without the customer opt-out); technical and operational support performed exclusively within the Union (levels 3-4: by Union residents and non-third-country-controlled parties).
obligations.conditional_on: Recognition at Union assurance level 2, 3 or 4

evidence.quote: the technical and operational support or assistance related to the audited service, including subsequent sub-outsourcing arrangements, are initiated and performed exclusively within the Union;

obligations.summary: Levels 2-3 require a European cybersecurity certificate of at least assurance level 'substantial' (level 4: 'high') under a Cybersecurity Act cloud scheme once established; until then national schemes, or else the highest cybersecurity standards under Union law.
obligations.conditional_on: Recognition at Union assurance level 2, 3 or 4

evidence.quote: the audited service obtains a European cybersecurity certificate of at least assurance level ‘high’ under a European cybersecurity certification scheme covering cloud computing services

obligations.summary: Levels 2-4: data generated by using the service may not be used to train or fine-tune any AI system operated by a third country or third-country entity, nor transferred outside the Union.
obligations.conditional_on: Recognition at Union assurance level 2, 3 or 4

evidence.quote: the data generated by using the audited service are not used to train or fine-tune any AI system operated by a third country or a legal entity established in a third-country

obligations.summary: Level 2: a third-country-controlled provider must show legal, technical and organisational measures preventing third-country control from restricting the service, accessing customer data, disrupting or degrading service, or imposing third-country restrictive measures.
obligations.conditional_on: Recognition at level 2 by a provider subject to third-country control

evidence.quote: access by a third country or by a legal entity established in a third-country to customer data is prevented;

obligations.summary: Levels 3-4: provider and involved subcontractors must not be subject to third-country control; at level 3 a derogation applies for providers controlled from a third country named by Commission implementing act (Art. 18), with separation safeguards and reasonable access to code.
obligations.conditional_on: Recognition at Union assurance level 3 or 4

evidence.quote: the audited provider and the subcontractors which are involved in the provision of the audited service are not subject to the control of a third country or a legal entity established in a third-country;

obligations.summary: Levels 3-4: personnel (including subcontractors') involved in the service must be Union citizens, with Member State security clearance where handling classified information; at level 2 citizenship and screening apply only if the public sector body requires them.
obligations.conditional_on: Recognition at Union assurance level 3 or 4 (level 2 on request of the public body)

evidence.quote: the personnel, including the personnel of the subcontractors , which are involved in the provision of the audited service are Union citizens and, where appropriate, the personnel must also have the necessary national security clearance

obligations.summary: Levels 2-4: software supply-chain measures (SBOM and dependency list for the auditor; controls blocking remote tamper features; source-code audits and migration plans for third-country components; level 4: effective control over software components) and controls on open-source software.
obligations.conditional_on: Recognition at Union assurance level 2, 3 or 4

evidence.quote: a complete and up-to-date software bill of materials ( SBOM ) , as defined in Article 3 , point (39) , of Regulation (EU) 2024/2847, and a list of identified dependencies

obligations.summary: Levels 2-4: providers operating globally with a third-country subsidiary must ensure effective legal, technical and organisational separation between the Union parent and the subsidiary.
obligations.conditional_on: Recognition at level 2, 3 or 4 by a provider with a third-country subsidiary

evidence.quote: the audited provider has implemented the necessary measures to ensure and enforce the effective legal, technical and organisational separation between the Union parent company and any such third-country subsidiary

obligations.summary: The Commission must establish and maintain a public central repository of recognised cloud computing services, where revocations stay published for five years.

evidence.quote: The Commission shall establish and maintain a dedicated repository of cloud computing services that have been recogni sed in accordance with A rticle 1 7

evidence.quote: The national competent authority of establishment that recognised a cloud computing service under Article 1 7 shall register the cloud computing service in the central repository.

obligations.summary: Member States must lay down effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties for infringements of the cloud sovereignty Chapter, weighing the Art. 24(2) criteria, and notify them to the Commission.

evidence.quote: Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of this Chapter by cloud computing service providers within their competence

obligations.summary: Member States must designate national competent authorities, notify them to the Commission, and give them sufficient resources; the Member State of main establishment has exclusive enforcement competence.

evidence.quote: shall have exclusive competence for enforc ing this Chapter .

obligations.summary: Competent authorities must give mutual assistance and answer information requests within two months, and the authority of establishment must assess requests from authorities of destination or the Commission and report within two months.

evidence.quote: The competent authority receiving the request pursuant to paragraph 2 shall comply with such request

obligations.summary: Member States and Union entities must carry out risk assessments identifying public sector activities using cloud services that contribute to public order and the Union assurance level (2, 3 or 4) appropriate to each, considering data sensitivity, unlawful third-country access, disruption risk and multi-cloud strategies.

‘cloud computing service’ means cloud computing service as defined in Article 6 , point (30) , of Directive (EU) 2022/2555

‘AI system’ means an AI system as defined in Article 3 , point (1) , of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
‘frontier AI’ means AI models or AI systems built upon such models that can perform a wide variety of tasks and that approach, reach or exceed the current state of the art
‘AI agent’ means an AI system or a coordinated set of AI systems, that can perceive and act upon their environment, with a degree of autonomy, using tools as needed to achieve specific goals
‘public sector body’ means public sector body as defined in Article 2, point (1), of Directive (EU) 2019/1024
‘Union entities’ means the Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies set up by or pursuant to the Treaty on European Union
means a small or medium-sized enterprise as defined in Article 2 of Annex I to Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC

‘software’ means software as defined in Article 3, point (4), of Regulation (EU) 2024/2847

‘control’ means control as defined in Article 2 , point (6) , of Regulation (EU) 2021/697
‘contracting authorities’ means contracting authorities as defined in Article 2(1), point (1) , of Directive 2014/24/EU
source licence’ means open source licence as defined in Article 2, point (12), of Regulation (EU) 2024/903
large-scale, cross-sectoral initiatives addressing major technological and industrial challenges of strategic relevan ce for the Union (‘ g rand c hallenges’)

where the cloud computing service provider has its head office or registered office from which the principal financial functions and operational control are exercised

notes: Neutral annotation of a pending Commission proposal; obligations describe what would apply. Vocabulary gaps: cloud computing service providers are coded as 'data_processor' (no cloud-provider role exists); auditing organisations (duties in Art. 20(3)-(6)) and NIS2 private entities that a delegated act could require to carry out impact assessments (Art. 31(3)) have no matching addressee role and are described here rather than as obligation rows. Annex II criteria are coded as obligations conditional on seeking each assurance level. Open delegated and implementing acts: Centres for AI procedure (Art. 5(4)), amendments to Annex I (Art. 6(4)) and Annexes II-III (Arts 16(2), 21(1)), audit rules (Art. 20(9)), associated third countries (Art. 18), recognition arrangements (Art. 17(12)), risk-assessment methodology (Art. 29(3)), EuroCloud and procurement fees (Arts 34-36, 40). Annex I targets (average PUE 1.15, server utilisation towards 50%) are grand-challenge aims, not legal thresholds, and are not coded. Text inconsistencies: two articles are numbered 44 (OSPO Network; Exercise of the delegation), while Art. 6(4), 16(2), 20(9), 21(1) and 31(3) refer to 'Article 45' for delegated acts; Annex II 3.1(g) and Annex III 7.2(c) refer to an implementing act 'under Article 19' for associated third countries, which Art. 18 governs; Art. 2 definitions skip from (22) to (25); Art. 30(4) lists points (a), (b), (a); Art. 26(2)(c) links periodic penalty payments to Art. 24.
